Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, lobulated soft-tissue mass occupying the right hemithorax, which is characteristic of a pleural or chest wall sarcoma such as a pleomorphic liposarcoma. This appearance distinguishes it from the diffuse opacities of pneumonia or fibrosis, the air-fluid levels/meniscus of effusion, or the lucency of pneumothorax; Figure 1c shows the post-resection state confirming it was a discrete resectable mass.
